evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0h = 11.71 mg/L, well above the 2.0 mg/L minimum; no downward oxygen trend (values 40–52h stable around 12–13 mg/L)
Receiving P assay: 1.14 g/L (36h), 3.16 g/L (48h) — consistent with healthy source batches (P ~1.0–1.1 at 36h, ~3.0 at 48h), indicating a normal production trajectory
Feed-induced DO dips to ~9.4 mg/L at 24h recover fully, as in source batches; no evidence of oxygen constraint
No abnormal divergence between receiving and source trajectories that would motivate feed or air changes
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation at t=52 h is tracking the healthy source-batch trajectory closely. Receiving DO2 (~11.7 mg/L) is far above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint and shows no decline toward limitation. Product trajectory (P=1.14 g/L at 36 h, 3.16 g/L at 48 h available at 40/52 h) matches the source batches (1.0–1.1 at 36 h, 3.0–3.1 at 48 h) which go on to reach ~8 g/L peak around 72–84 h. There is no evidence of oxygen stress, byproduct accumulation, or divergence that would justify reducing feed, increasing air, or stopping. A stop would forfeit the substantial remaining product formation (sources gain ~5 g/L from 48 h to peak). Feed reduction would unnecessarily lower productivity; increased air provides no benefit since DO2 is not constrained. KEEP is the bounded, lowest-risk intervention that retains full product mass.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process parameters may differ from source processes, so future DO2 could fall faster than sources; but with ~10 mg/L headroom over the constraint and no adverse trend, risk of a KEEP violation is low. The 52 h P assay (3.16 g/L) is a 48 h sample, so the last 4 h of state are unobserved; DO2 sensor at 52 h remains healthy, which mitigates this. If a sharp DO2 decline appeared later, increase_air would be the fallback, but current evidence does not support it.
